title: Parliament House & Constitution of India
shortDescription: A living promise of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
description: The Constituent Assembly, chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, began drafting India's constitution in December 1946 in the Central Hall of Parliament House. The Drafting Committee, headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, shaped the sovereign text establishing India as a democratic republic. This interactive 3D model presents the monumental circular Parliament House in New Delhi where India's constitutional journey was born.
keyFacts: Constituent Assembly deliberations ran from December 1946 to November 1949
Adopted on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas)
Came into force on 26 January 1950, marked as Republic Day
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee
The original handwritten copies were calligraphed by Prem Behari Narain Raizada and illustrated by artists from Shantiniketan
The longest written constitution of any sovereign country

title: ISRO Achievements
shortDescription: A story of space science built around practical problem-solving and public purpose.
description: India's space effort began modestly in 1963 with a sounding rocket launched from Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, under the guidance of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. The Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), formed in 1962, was reorganised into the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on 15 August 1969. Sarabhai believed space technology should serve national development rather than prestige alone — a philosophy that still shapes ISRO's mission mix.
keyFacts: INCOSPAR founded in 1962; reorganised as ISRO on 15 August 1969
Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme
India's first sounding rocket was launched from Thumba in 1963
Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was built by ISRO and launched in 1975
PSLV became renowned for exceptional reliability and low-cost launches
Mangalyaan (2013) made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt

title: Statue of Unity
shortDescription: The world's tallest monument honouring the political integration of India.
description: Rising 182 metres along the Narmada river facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam, the Statue of Unity commemorates Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India who united 562 princely states into the sovereign Indian union. This interactive 3D model presents the world-record colossus in its engineering detail.
keyFacts: Inaugurated on 31 October 2018, the 143rd birth anniversary of Sardar Patel
World's tallest statue with a height of 182 metres (597 feet)
Designed by renowned Indian sculptor Ram V. Sutar
Engineered to withstand winds of up to 180 km/h and high-magnitude earthquakes
Built with over 70,000 tonnes of cement, 18,500 tonnes of reinforcement steel and 1,700 tonnes of bronze plates

title: Chandrayaan Missions
shortDescription: Lunar exploration that placed Indian science at the centre of a new space age.
description: Chandrayaan-1, launched on 22 October 2008 aboard a PSLV rocket, orbited the Moon and helped confirm water molecules on the lunar surface. Chandrayaan-3, launched on 14 July 2023 aboard the LVM3 rocket, achieved history: its Vikram lander touched down in the Moon's south polar highlands on 23 August 2023 at 6:04 pm IST, deploying the Pragyan rover. The achievement made India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to do so near the lunar south pole.
keyFacts: Chandrayaan-1 launched 22 October 2008; confirmed water molecules on the Moon
Chandrayaan-3 launched 14 July 2023 on the LVM3 rocket from Sriharikota
Vikram lander soft-landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, at 6:04 pm IST
India became the first nation to land in the lunar south polar region
23 August is officially commemorated in India as National Space Day

title: Digital India
shortDescription: Infrastructure and public services imagined for a connected, mobile-first nation.
description: Launched on 1 July 2015, Digital India is built around three vision areas: digital infrastructure as a core utility for every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment through literacy and universal access. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched by NPCI in 2016, enabled instant digital payments at massive scale.
keyFacts: Officially launched on 1 July 2015
Built on nine pillars, including broadband highways and e-Kranti
UPI, launched in 2016 by NPCI, enabled interoperable real-time digital payments
Aadhaar and DigiLocker provide universal digital identity and document infrastructure
